test_title: PYST 35: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 2 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

One should __________ one’s promises.
solution:
The correct option to** fill in the blank is 2) keep.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To keep one's promises **means** to fulfill the commitment that one has made to someone.**
 
• It implies that a person is trustworthy and reliable.
 
• For instance, if you promise to meet your friend at a particular time, keeping the promise means arriving at the designated time.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Sarah always **keeps her promises**, no matter how busy she is.
 
 
 
• **"Keep a promise"** is a common collocation. Collocations are words that frequently occur together in language use. They often form a more natural and meaningful expression than using individual words.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Correct Sentence:**__ *One should **__keep__*** *one’s promises.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) take** is not appropriate as it does not convey the meaning of fulfilling a commitment. It rather means to adopt or assume something.
 
• Example:
 
 
• I will **take **your advice and try to improve my performance.
 
 
 
• **Option 3) hide **is entirely incorrect as it has no connection to promises. It means to conceal something or keep it secret.
 
• Example:
 
 
• He tried to **hide **his mistake, but it was eventually discovered.
 
 
 
• **Option 4) give **is also not suitable as it does not convey the idea of fulfilling a commitment. It means to transfer something to someone else.
 
• Example:
 
 
• She **gave** me a book as a birthday present.
